title: Acts, again
tomorrow: Paul's 'charity is patient' wasn't written for a wedding. so who for?

cards: Every group project has someone everyone underestimates: the quiet one, the new one. Then they stand up to present, and the room goes still. In Acts, the room is the council in Jerusalem.
Peter and John, two fishermen, are standing in front of it after a man who couldn't walk has gotten up at the Temple gate.
The leaders look them over, and in the Douay-Rheims Bible, "understanding that they were illiterate and ignorant men, they wondered." They order them to stop speaking in the name of Jesus.
And the two of them say they can't.

teach.b: Their answer, in the same old translation: "For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard."
And the council notices one more thing, the reason behind the nerve: these two had been with Jesus. That's Acts in a sentence.
It's the second half of Luke's story, and it opens with a promise: the Holy Spirit will come, and they'll be witnesses in Jerusalem, then farther, to the ends of the earth.
Then it happens at Pentecost, and the sending begins. Look who gets sent. Not a team of experts.

A man named Philip, picked to help hand out food, sent down a desert road to explain scripture to a stranger in a chariot. Ordinary people, moved along by the Spirit, often to places they didn't plan to go.

Something to tell a friend tonight: the Latin Mass ends with the words ite, missa est, a dismissal, go. Some readers hear the very name Mass in that sending. Every Mass, in that reading, ends the way Acts begins.

how: Catholics hear the Acts of the Apostles read at Mass through the Easter season, and every Mass ends with the people being sent out.

games.q: the sent ones — tap the pairs.

s: the council in Acts sees Peter and John as unlettered men, and wonders at their nerve.
when ordered to stop, Peter and John say they cannot
we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.
in Acts, only the twelve apostles are sent
others are sent too: Philip, picked to help with food, goes down a desert road.

games.q: your cousin got asked to help lead the parish youth retreat, and she wants to say no because she 'isn't the type.' what does Acts suggest?
o: the type in Acts is ordinary people moved by the Spirit.
leave it to people with theology degrees and training.
only go if a clear sign shows up first.
games.why: the council saw fishermen with no schooling, and wondered. Philip was picked to hand out food and then sent down a desert road.

practice: Stand up and walk slowly, even across one room, for a minute. With each step, name a place you'll be today: a class, a job, a kitchen, a bus. Then sit for the rest, and ask to be useful in one of those places, or simply hope to be.

wordCard.voice: Acts. The Acts of the Apostles: ordinary people, sent by the Spirit, who could not stop speaking.

orig.note: Greek: apostle, one sent out; the word in the book's title.
